title: Apollinarius and Nestorius share one impiety
english: I consider the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius to be one and the same impiety. I believe it is the same error to ascribe division or a duality to the Only-Begotten Son of God according to the incarnation, and not to confess that his flesh, which has a soul and is all-holy, is human except for sin alone. It is the same error to say either that his flesh had its existence from heaven, or that it came into being through a change of the Word. To those who have fallen into any such error, I say, quoting Scripture, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures (Matthew 22:29).”

added_allusions.reason: Recorded (justifications/frag-open.json, method: wording). The papyrus reads Planontai me eidotes tas graphas (You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures), the saying of Matthew 22:29, planasthe me eidotes tas graphas, recast as a direct address inside the quoted saying, where the citation is inlined. Mark 12:24's parallel was considered and not added: the papyrus lacks Mark's distinctive opening.
